Q: Nominating only a table name when calling CodeIgniter's insert() fails to insert a row A:

You're missing an argument - insert() takes two:

  1. A table name
  2. An array or object containing columns and values

From the documentation:

$data = array(
   'title' => 'My title' ,
   'name' => 'My Name' ,
   'date' => 'My date'
);

$this->db->insert('mytable', $data); 

// Produces: INSERT INTO mytable (title, name, date) VALUES ('My title', 'My name', 'My date')

So, you need to supply insert() with the necessary data by including an array or object as the second argument.

Edit:

Alternatively, you can use the $this->db->set() method for setting values, as explained in Rocket's more comprehensive answer, which also points out you need to specify a table when selecting data.

Q: What are the mechanics of custom CMake install()-command scripts? A:

The code specified in the install(CODE) signature will be executed as part of a CMake script generated for the project's installation. It will be executed in scripting mode, without access to the context (functions, variables, targets) of the project's CMakeLists.txt:

  1. cmake processes project's CMakeLists.txt in its own context, and generates build scripts and cmake_install.cmake installation script.
  2. make install (or corresponding command for other build tool) executes cmake -P cmake_install.cmake.

Whatever data you want to pass from the CMakeLists.txt to the code specified via install(CODE) should be embedded into that code. E.g. by dereferencing of variables when define such code:

set(project_mode cool)
...
install(CODE "message(\"Install project in mode ${project_mode}.\")")

The installation code defined by such script will contain the line

message("Install project in mode cool.")

In such code only commands from the scripting list may be used.

E.g. that list lacks for add_subdirectory command, because scripting mode lacks for concept of source and build directories.

install command is inaccessible in the installation code too. For create files, use file command.
